title: Commodity-specific critical minerals evidence for future systems
question: Which materials are binding for chips, grids, batteries, defense, and AI infrastructure?
why_it_matters: Critical minerals matter differently across systems. FTFN needs commodity-specific evidence before treating a material as a binding constraint.
current_support: FTFN now has the USGS 2026 report and machine-readable 2025 production, trade, and import-reliance baseline alongside named award and project trails.
missing_evidence: project sites, permits, and physical progress
candidate_records: DOE Critical Minerals and Materials Accelerator opportunity
next_action: Pair the selected gallium and Talon Nickel records with trade, permitting, facility, commissioning, production, inventory, qualification, and offtake evidence before treating either material or project as a binding system constraint.
notes: Phase 55Z adds current commodity outcomes without claiming facility-level supply security or qualified output.
